description.narrative:
Overall Objective: To strengthen peer learning, collaboration, and youth-led advocacy among AU–EU Youth Action Lab grantees by facilitating and moderating the Power to Voices digital platform, supported by a team of experienced youth facilitators drawn from CODE’s Follow the Money (FTM) accountability and advocacy network.
Specific Objectives 1. Build an active and inclusive online community: To establish a safe, well-moderated Power to Voices platform where Youth Action Lab grantees regularly engage, share experiences, and learn from one another through structured facilitation and peer support. 2. Strengthen peer-to-peer learning across cohorts: To promote meaningful learning and exchange between Cohort 1 and Cohort 2 grantees through online sessions, peer discussions, and collaborative activities grounded in community-level youth action. 3. Support youth-led advocacy and influencing: To strengthen the ability of grantees to collaborate digitally,create advocacy content, and engage decision-makers through People’s Parliament-style dialogues and shared learning activities.
Key Activities: Month 1 – Project Inception and Onboarding: The project will begin with onboarding of Cohort 2 grantees onto the Power to Voices platform, platform orientation, and agreement on community guidelines. A baseline capacity and needs assessment will be conducted to guide learning design and facilitation. Month 2 – Thematic Learning and CommunityEngagement: The first thematic online learning session will be delivered based on identified needs. Facilitated discussions and regular content sharing will encourage participation and knowledge exchange across the platform. Month 3 – Peer Learning and People’s Parliament Dialogue:A peer learning exchange between Cohort1 and Cohort 2 grantees will be organised, followed by aPeople’s Parliament-style dialogue on governance, education, and other relevant deep-rooted issues to support collective reflection, shared problem-solving, and youth-led advocacy discussions. Month4 – Virtual Youth Hackathon (Ideation Phase): A virtual youth hackathon will bring together grantees from Africa and Europe to develop ideas addressing shared challenges, with guidance provided through structured facilitation and peer mentoring. Month 5– Hackathon Mentorship and Skills Development: Hackathon teams will receive mentoring support and participate in an online skills-building workshop focused on solution development, collaboration, and advocacy planning. Month 6 – Mid-Cycle Reflection andCapacity Development: A mid-cycle reflection session will assess progress, participation levels, and learning outcomes, and inform adjustments to facilitation and content delivery. Month 7 – AU–EU Thematic Exchange and Storytelling: An AU–EU thematic exchange will connect grantees across regions, followed by a storytelling workshop to support the development of digital narratives and shared learning content. Month 8 – Second Youth Hackathon and Solution Testing: A second hackathon will focus on refining and testing solutions, with participants applying lessons learned from earlier sessions and peer exchanges. Month 9 – Advocacy and Influencing Dialogue: An advocacy-focused People’s Parliament dialogue will support youth-led discussion on influencing pathways and engagement with decision-makers. Month 10 – Peer Exchange and Collaboration Showcase: Grantees will participate in a collaboration showcase to share joint initiatives, lessons learned, and emerging practices. Month 11 – Learning Documentation and Amplification: Key learning outputs, stories, and reflections will be documented on the platform and shared through digital channels to amplify youth voices. Month 12 – Final Reflection, Reporting, and Sustainability Planning: The project will conclude with reflection sessions, final reporting, and sustainability planning to support continued peer learning beyond the project period.

participating-org.narrative:
Connected Development (CODE) a youth-led, non-profit organisation working to amplify youth voices, strengthen civic participation, and promote inclusive and sustainable development across Nigeria and beyond. CODE envisions a world where the rights of all people are upheld and protected, reflecting its commitment to a just, equitable, and accountable society.
CODE’s mission is to advance innovative solutions for the sustainable development of marginalized and vulnerable groups through transparency, accountability, and gender equity in the protection of their political, socio-economic, and environmental rights. The organisation pursues this mission by leveraging youth leadership, digital innovation, storytelling, and evidence-based advocacy to connect communities particularly youngpeople to decision-makers and development processes.
A core objective of CODE is to strengthen transparency and accountability in governance while promoting gender inclusion,social justice, and meaningful youth participation. Through its flagship iFollowTheMoneydigital platform, CODE mobilises over9,000 active volunteers nationwide, enabling youth-led monitoring of public resources, advocacy campaigns, and community engagement initiatives that hold duty-bearers accountable and amplify grassroots voices.
CODE has a strong record of mobilising young people through online platforms, peer-learning exchanges, civic innovation, and policy advocacy that advance democratic governance and inclusive development outcomes. The organisation also maintains a robust digital presence, with over 71,000 followers across X (Twitter), Facebook, LinkedIn, and Instagram, which it uses for youth engagement, learning, advocacy, and public accountability.
CODE’s work is guided by strong institutional values, including integrity, respect, collaboration, transparency and accountability,empathy, and a results-oriented approach, which together provide an ethical framework for decision-making and stakeholder engagement. The organisation is governed and led by young people aged 18–35, in line with its founding principle of “Nothingabout youth, without youth."
